title: Precision Safeguard: INT8 GPTQ/AWQ Profile Integration and E2E Calibration Verification Pipeline
creator: Anika Rao
description: Integrate INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ and AWQ variants) into the CI/regression pipeline with an end-to-end calibration and accuracy verification harness. This ticket covers adding reproducible calibration runs, deterministic seed handling, golden prompt sets, and automated detection of accuracy regressions vs FP16 baselines. Goal: provide fast CI smoke checks and a nightly full calibration + evaluation job that gates PRs that touch quant code paths.
background: We already have ad-hoc scripts for generating INT8 weight-only profiles, but coverage is inconsistent across model families (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder) and quant backends. Recent incidents surfaced a subtle bias introduced by one AWQ packing variant that passed unit tests but regressed end-user perplexity on a small set of prompts. This work aims to create a repeatable pipeline that catches similar regressions before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A CI smoke job exists that runs GPTQ and AWQ weight-only profile generation for a small model (7B) and validates token-logprobs on a golden prompt set within 1.5% of FP16 baseline for head-0..3 and across three random seeds.
A nightly job runs full calibration + evaluation for target models (7B, 13B, 34B) and publishes per-model accuracy reports to the console dashboard and an S3 bucket in CSV format.
Regression detection: any nightly run with >1.5% drop in mean logprob or a shift in top-1 token stats triggers an automated Linear regression alert and opens a rollback candidate PR template.
Deterministic calibration artifacts (profile files + seed metadata) are archived and accessible via stable S3 paths for forensic reproduction.
The pipeline runs in <30 minutes for the CI smoke job and <3 hours for the nightly jobs on Dedicated test pool hardware, and resource requests/limits are documented.
Docs: brief runbook added in Confluence with troubleshooting steps, and a sample PR checklist for engineers touching quant paths.
Unit/e2e tests included in the PR: baseline comparisons must be run with fixed random seeds and log artifacts uploaded to the test run for review.
tasks: Add new CI workflow file (buildkite) for 'int8-quant-smoke' that executes profile generation + lightweight eval
Implement deterministic seed handling in quant toolchain and surface seed in profile metadata
Create golden prompt set (50 prompts) with diversified tokens (numerics, punctuation, long-tail names) and store in repo/test-data
Wire evaluation harness to compute per-token logprobs and summary metrics (mean logprob, top-1 accuracy, KL divergence) vs FP16 baseline
Provision nightly runner on dedicated test GPUs and S3 archiving with lifecycle policy for artifacts
Add regression alerting: compare nightly results against historical baseline and create Linear issue when threshold exceeded
Update docs/runbook and add PR checklist items for quant-related changes
Coordinate with Model Onboarding team for model list and acceptable thresholds per-family
test_plan: CI smoke: run on PRs that touch /quant/ or /runtime/ paths. Use 3 seeds, single-batch generation, compare to stored FP16 baseline file. Fail PR if mean logprob drop >1.5%

Nightly: generate full INT8 profiles for target models using both GPTQ and AWQ pipelines; run 10k token eval across golden prompts; upload CSV and JSONL artifacts to S3 path s3://redwood-quant-artifacts/ENG-17012/nightly/YYYYMMDD/
Regression verification: on flagged runs, automatically kick off a deterministic rerun with an alternate seed set and collect diff report; only open regression ticket if rerun confirms the drop
Performance gating: measure CI smoke runtime and memory; ensure smoke job uses a constrained batch size and sequence length to bound runtime under 30 minutes
notes: Decision: keep both GPTQ and AWQ as separate branches in the harness to capture packing-implementation divergences
Trade-off: nightly full calibrations are expensive; to mitigate cost we will tier models (7B nightly, 13B every 2 nights, 34B weekly) after 2 weeks of baseline data
Implementation detail: use deterministic CUDA/cuBLAS seeds + numpy/randomstate for Python-level randomness to guarantee reproducibility across runners
Fallback: on alert, pipeline should optionally run a rerun with different seed set to confirm flakiness before creating regression ticket
